candidates.summary: A tribunal rules public money spent on safety work at seven blocks in Manchester should be repaid
candidates.reason: Cheap pre-enrich duplicate — same URL/title kept from stronger source.
candidates.practical_angle: Проверить, есть ли действующие ограничения по дыму или дорожные закрытия сегодня.
candidates.lead: A tribunal rules public money spent on safety work at seven blocks in Manchester should be repaid
candidates.evidence_text: A building developer has been ordered to pay more than £45m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. A spokesperson said the scale of the liability was "significant" The Department of Housing, Communities and Local Government brought a case to a specialist tribunal, seeking an order for the developer to contribute towards the cost of the works paid from the taxpayer-supported fund On Thursday, the tribunal ruled that more than £45.7m should be paid to the government by Urban Splash
candidates.what_happened: Developer Urban Splash forced to pay £45m over Manchester fire safety works
candidates.source_evidence: The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. A spokesperson said the scale of the liability was "significant" The Department of Housing, Communities and Local Government brought a case to a specialist tribunal, seeking an order for the developer to contribute towards the cost of the works paid from the taxpayer-supported fund On Thursday, the tribunal ruled that more than £45.7m should be paid to the government by Urban Splash Judge Jonathan Holbrook, sitting with two other First Tier Tribunal members, said in a 260-page judgment there was a "powerful case" for the developer "rather than the taxpayer, to bear the remediation costs"

candidates.evidence_text: A small food shed set up on a driveway in Cheshire less than two years ago has grown into a community hub which helps about 200 people each week Sutton Community Fridge was set up in December 2024 by Gayle Parks to tackle food waste and help families in the Macclesfield area access affordable food The project collects surplus stock from supermarkets, charities and businesses that would otherwise be thrown away and makes it available to buy at a low price The idea came to Gayle after about £15,000 worth of stock was stolen during a burglary at her family's pet shop In the aftermath, she relied on apps offering surplus food to help feed her own family She said: ''It made me question how could perfectly good food be going to waste when families were struggling to put food on their tables?''

candidates.title: Man hit by bus in Stockport missed granddaughter's birth by a day
candidates.summary: Ross Grealey's children said their father was "one of a kind" and loved by many
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: Ross Grealey's children said their father was "one of a kind" and loved by many
candidates.evidence_text: Man hit by bus in Stockport missed granddaughter's birth by a day - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Carla Grealey said her father Ross was "one of a kind" and loved by many By Haider Saleem North West Published 5 November 2026 The family of a man who died after being hit by a bus in Greater Manchester said they were heartbroken he missed the birth of his granddaughter by just one day. Ross Grealey died after he was struck near Winifred Road in Stockport on 30 October, Greater Manchester Police said. His son, who is also called Ross, said a baby girl was born the following day and wished his father had been able to meet her. His daughter Carla Grealey described her father as "one of a kind" and said he was loved by many. In a tribute his son said: "You're now a grandad to a beautiful baby girl, who was born just a day after this tragedy. I wish with all my heart that you could have met her." "A little piece of you will live on through her," he said. Carla added: "I'm truly heartbroken. I still can't understand any of it. I just wish it hadn't happened." Staff at The Wellspring, who supported Grealey, said he was always ready with a story, a smile and a hug. "He made our world a better place simply by being in it," the team said. candidates.evidence_text: Pat Karney funeral: Andy Burnham says he shaped Manchester - BBC News Image caption, Prime Minister Andy Burnham joined mourners at St Mary's Roman Catholic Church to pay his respects to Pat Karney By Richard Stead , Kaya Black , Reporting from Manchester and Haider Saleem , North West Published 5 November 2026 Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described long-serving Manchester councillor Pat Karney as a "political genius" at his funeral, saying his "spirit is in every street" of the city. Burnham, who worked alongside the Labour politician for 25 years, told mourners: "I loved Pat and I looked up to him and I will miss him as we all will." Karney, who represented Harpurhey in north Manchester from 1979, died on 13 October aged 78 . He was known for championing the city's major celebrations and played a significant role in its political life. Before the service, his hearse paused in Albert Square, where a Ferris wheel displayed the message "Thank You Pat" beside the city's Christmas Markets. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, Karney's funeral cortege paused in Albert Square, where he helped champion Manchester's Christmas Markets The funeral cortege passed Manchester Town Hall before continuing to the church, known as the Hidden Gem, on Mulberry Street. The service began at 10:00 GMT, with Abide with Me the first hymn. During his funeral address, Burnham recalled the many sides of Karney, from his political campaigning to his sense of humour and love of celebrations. "He knew in his bones how much Manchester likes a party," he said. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, The PM paid tribute to Pat Karney, describing the long-serving councillor as a "political genius" Burnham recalled once raising concerns about the Christmas Markets starting earlier each year, only for Karney to tell him: "Andy, I'll start them in July if I could." He also praised Karney's political influence, describing him as the "godfather of the most successful Labour group in the country". Image source, Manchester City Council Image caption, Pat Karney represented Harpurhey on Manchester City Council from 1979 until his death in October He said Karney had been instrumental in resolving disagreements within the Labour group and had played an important part in the city's transformation. The prime minister also recalled Karney's involvement in campaigning against anti-LGBT legislation in the 1980s and his dedication to the people of Harpurhey. "Pat shaped this place. His spirit is in every street," he said. Image caption, Lucy Powell remembered Karney's sense of fun and his contribution to Manchester's regeneration Education Secretary Lucy Powell, the MP for Manchester Central, said Karney "wouldn't have wanted us all to be sad today". She said he would have wanted people to remember his personality, sense of fun and love for the city. But Powell said there had also been a serious side to his work, particularly his involvement in regenerating Manchester city centre. Image caption, Labour MP Jeff Smith was among those attending the funeral in Manchester city centre Former Manchester City Council leader Sir Richard Leese, who worked alongside Karney for decades, echoed those sentiments. "What's often not acknowledged is he was a very, very serious politician," he said. Sir Richard said Karney had been central to major decisions during his 25 years as council leader, including Manchester's recovery from the 1996 IRA bombing and its response to the Covid pandemic. He also recalled how Karney would not accept criticism of the city. Image caption, Friends and political colleagues gathered in Albert Square ahead of Pat Karney's funeral service Image caption, Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds was among the political figures paying their respects to Karney People gathered outside the church, known locally as the Hidden Gem, to watch the invitation-only service on a large screen. Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds was among those paying their respects. Karney had served on Manchester City Council since 1979 and was closely associated with the city's major celebrations. Its Christmas Markets are due to open on Friday, the first time the event has taken place since his death. Image caption, Pallbearers carried Pat Karney's coffin into St Mary's Roman Catholic Church, known locally as the Hidden Gem Image caption

candidates.evidence_text: Man catches thief with Apple AirTag hidden in stone - BBC News Image caption, Matt Smith says people were "miffed" with stones being taken so he had to take action By Emma Stanley North West Published 5 November 2026 A thief who was stealing a wall piece by piece was caught when a man put a tracking device in one of the stones. Matt Smith said people living near Rufford Old Hall in Lancashire, "were getting a bit miffed" with stones being taken from the 300-year-old boundary wall. So he put an Apple AirTag - a coin-sized tracking device people attach to keys or wallets in case they lose them - inside one of the stones. Police followed the trail to an address in Wigan, and earlier this month, a man pleaded guilty at Wigan Magistrates' Court to two counts of theft and one count of handling stolen goods. Last October, about 30 stones went missing from a half-mile-long stretch of road which connects Holmeswood and Rufford. "We looked at installing some CCTV, but it costs and with the wall being attacked at random places at random times, in a half mile stretch of wall, it was going to be hard to cover that area," Smith, a parish councillor, told BBC Radio Lancashire. Image source, Lancashire Police Image caption, About 30 stones had gone missing from along a half-mile-long stretch of road which connects Holmeswood and Rufford He added: "So we put some lovely 'smile you're on camera' signs up and unfortunately that didn't deter them. "So I devised a plan and spoke with the owners. "We'd noticed it was the smaller of the stones that were being taken, so we put a tracking device in what we thought would maybe be the next stone to be taken. "So there was a bit of guesswork involved." Smith said he "lifted a couple of the smaller coping stones off, core drilled into the bottom of those and placed in an Apple AirTag, patched up the core, ground it up, put a bit of resin in" and placed it back on the wall. "Lo and behold, four weeks later my phone started to ping with the tracking device on the move to an address in Winstanley in Wigan," he said. He contacted the police, who went to the address and made an arrest. The coping stones were later returned and the "extremely grateful" residents rebuilt the wall. Last month, Craig Barker, 41, from Wigan, pleaded guilty to theft and handling stolen goods and was given a 12-month sentence, suspended for 22 months. PC Sean Dalby, of the South Rural Task Force, said: "This case highlights the strong relationships we have developed with our communities and demonstrates the effectiveness of working together to tackle rural and heritage crime. "I would like to thank the local residents for their support throughout the investigation, as well as those who gave their time to rebuild the wall free of charge." candidates.evidence_text: A small food shed set up on a driveway in Cheshire less than two years ago has grown into a community hub which helps about 200 people each week Sutton Community Fridge was set up in December 2024 by Gayle Parks to tackle food waste and help families in the Macclesfield area access affordable food The project collects surplus stock from supermarkets, charities and businesses that would otherwise be thrown away and makes it available to buy at a low price The idea came to Gayle after about £15,000 worth of stock was stolen during a burglary at her family's pet shop In the aftermath, she relied on apps offering surplus food to help feed her own family She said: ''It made me question how could perfectly good food be going to waste when families were struggling to put food on their tables?''

candidates.evidence_text: Real Life Manchester nurse's desperate bid to save husband, 41, who collapsed and died ended up saving three others Brion tragically died at just 41 years old after complaining of a headache Add to preferred sources Comments News James Besanvalle and A dad who collapsed then died after complaining of a headache has given the gift of life to others Bindhu Brion Xavier, 51, a nurse living in Manchester, said her husband first complained of a headache in the early afternoon of November 16 2014, for which she gave him both paracetamol and ibuprofen. But by 11pm her husband, Brion Xavier, then 41, a professional driver, complai While Bindhu was on the phone to emergency services, she said she heard a “snoring noise” and turned around to see her husband unconscious and unresponsive, with his tongue blocking his airway causing the sound, so she immediately began CPR Within minutes, paramedics arrived and performed further resuscitation on Brion, before they rushed him to hospital in Wythenshawe. He stayed in ICU for three days before brainstem testing confirmed the brain was no longer capable of supporting life due to a severe bleed While Bindhu tragically lost her husband, she was told that it was her quick response of CPR that meant Brion’s organs were able to be donated to save three people’s lives, including both of his kidneys and his liver

candidates.evidence_text: Carrington Carrington relief road has 1,000 against it and makes some 'ashamed to be human', but it will be happening The major relief road will unloock the wider redevelopment of Carrington and Partington and deliver thousands of new homes Add to pre The controversial Carrington relief road plan has been approved, despite hundreds of objections. For decades, the relief road has been seen as the solution to traffic woes in the Partington and Carrington areas of Trafford Diverting traffic away from the overly congested A6144 is seen as one of the major goals of the project. But when Trafford council tabled plans to finally deliver Carrington Relief Road, it caused uproar, with 680 letters of objection and a petition signed by over 1,000 people To get the very latest from Manchester's political scene in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Campaigners claimed the scheme will eat up a chunk of Carrington Moss nature reserve, destroying wildlife habitats and ecosystems along with it. Objectors also fear the plan could actually increase the number of cars passing through the area, with traffic from the nearby M60 and However, following a fractious council planning meeting on Thursday night (November 5), the scheme was narrowly approved by a vote of seven to six. Objectors in the public gallery could be heard shouting ‘it’s a disgrace’ following the decision

candidates.lead: Courts Screams as Audi driver smashes into cyclist before getting out and launching brutal attack Imran Hussain has been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 05:50, 06 Nov 2026 View Image Imran Hussain (Image: GMP) A driver rammed into a cyclist
candidates.evidence_text: Courts Screams as Audi driver smashes into cyclist before getting out and launching brutal attack Imran Hussain has been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 05:50, 06 Nov 2026 View Image Imran Hussain (Image: GMP) A driver rammed into a cyclist - pinning him against a van - before launching a 'deliberate and targeted attack'. Imran Hussain, 39, 'sped up' and drove into the man as he rode home from his girlfriend's house in June last year He hit the bike, pressing the rider against a parked van. As Hussain's victim screamed for help, he got out of his Audi and starting punching him in the head, Bolton Crown Court heard He then called out to his passenger to 'stab him' before they 'sliced' at the cyclist with a small blade. Hussain's accomplice has not been found The victim was left with two broken leg bones, cuts to his head and a partially-severed toe. Hussain was jailed for years and 10 months after pleading guilty to causing serious by dangerous driving; and section 18 wounding with intent The court earlier heard the man left his partner's home at around midnight on June 25. He was cycling to the shops when he got to the junction of Goldrill Avenue and Deepdale Road in Breightmet, Bolton. The men were 'known to one another, but the victim 'could see no reason why'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS Patients have been impacted by strikes at four Greater Manchester hospitals, trust bosses say as further walkouts loom in long-running overtime pay row Unison has hit back at the comments of Northern Care Alliance's interim chief executive, saying Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 16:58, 05 Nov 2026 Patients have been impacted by strikes at four Greater Manchester hospitals, an NHS trust has warned - with further walkouts expected amid a long-running dispute over overtime pay New figures published by Northern Care Alliance (NCA) - which runs Salford Royal, Royal Oldham , Rochdale Infirmary and Bury's Fairfield Hospital - report 12 incidents involving delays to treatment directly attributed to strikes Trust bosses said nearly half of the 28 incidents recorded due to treatment delays between July 1 and September 30 were directly caused by industrial action involving theatre staff Union bosses hit back, saying: "The power to prevent delays of treatments is in the hands of NCA's management." More than 350 theatre staff - including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers - have staged a number strikes in recent months amid a row over overtime payments

candidates.evidence_text: East Manchester Dispersal order issued for east Manchester as patrols stepped up ahead of Bonfire Night The order will be in place for 48 hours Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 16:58, 05 Nov 2026 View 2 Images Hyde Greater Manchester Police has issued a 48-hour dispersal order for an east Manchester district due to fears of anti-social behaviour over Bonfire Night The section 34 order will cover Gorton and Abbey Hey for 48 hours as of 1pm today (November 5) until 1pm on Saturday (November 7) It allows officers, who will be on patrol in the area, to direct people involved in or suspected of anti-social behaviour to leave the area for a specified period The force said the order for Gorton and Abbey Hey has been put in place due to concerns over 'the potential for bonfire-night related anti-social behaviour', which is said to have occurred 'in recent years' The area encompasses land between Ashton Old Road, Cornwall Street, Chapman Street, the A57/ Hyde Road, and across Debdale Park, Gorton Reservoir and Fairfield Golf Club

But by 11pm her husband, Brion Xavier, then 41, a professional driver, complai While Bindhu was on the phone to emergency services, she said she heard a “snoring noise” and turned around to see her husband unconscious and unresponsive, with his tongue blocking his airway causing the sound, so she immediately began CPR Within minutes, paramedics arrived and performed further resuscitation on Brion, before they rushed him to hospital in Wythenshawe. He stayed in ICU for three days before brainstem testing confirmed the brain was no longer capable of supporting life due to a severe bleed While Bindhu tragically lost her husband, she was told that it was her quick response of CPR that meant Brion’s organs were able to be donated to save three people’s lives, including both of his kidneys and his liver

But by 11pm her husband, Brion Xavier, then 41, a professional driver, complai While Bindhu was on the phone to emergency services, she said she heard a “snoring noise” and turned around to see her husband unconscious and unresponsive, with his tongue blocking his airway causing the sound, so she immediately began CPR Within minutes, paramedics arrived and performed further resuscitation on Brion, before they rushed him to hospital in Wythenshawe. He stayed in ICU for three days before brainstem testing confirmed the brain was no longer capable of supporting life due to a severe bleed While Bindhu tragically lost her husband, she was told that it was her quick response of CPR that meant Brion’s organs were able to be donated to save three people’s lives, including both of his kidneys and his liver

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Screams as Audi driver smashes into cyclist before getting out and launching brutal attack Imran Hussain has been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 05:50, 06 Nov 2026 View Image Imran Hussain (Image: GMP) A driver rammed into a cyclist - pinning him against a van - before launching a 'deliberate and targeted attack'. Imran Hussain, 39, 'sped up' and drove into the man as he rode home from his girlfriend's house in June last year He hit the bike, pressing the rider against a parked van. As Hussain's victim screamed for help, he got out of his Audi and starting punching him in the head, Bolton Crown Court heard He then called out to his passenger to 'stab him' before they 'sliced' at the cyclist with a small blade. Hussain's accomplice has not been found The victim was left with two broken leg bones, cuts to his head and a partially-severed toe. Hussain was jailed for years and 10 months after pleading guilty to causing serious by dangerous driving; and section 18 wounding with intent The court earlier heard the man left his partner's home at around midnight on June 25. He was cycling to the shops when he got to the junction of Goldrill Avenue and Deepdale Road in Breightmet, Bolton. The men were 'known to one another, but the victim 'could see no reason why'

Imran Hussain, 39, 'sped up' and drove into the man as he rode home from his girlfriend's house in June last year He hit the bike, pressing the rider against a parked van. As Hussain's victim screamed for help, he got out of his Audi and starting punching him in the head, Bolton Crown Court heard He then called out to his passenger to 'stab him' before they 'sliced' at the cyclist with a small blade. Hussain's accomplice has not been found The victim was left with two broken leg bones, cuts to his head and a partially-severed toe.

candidates.evidence_text: East Manchester Dispersal order issued for east Manchester as patrols stepped up ahead of Bonfire Night The order will be in place for 48 hours Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 16:58, 05 Nov 2026 View 2 Images Hyde Greater Manchester Police has issued a 48-hour dispersal order for an east Manchester district due to fears of anti-social behaviour over Bonfire Night The section 34 order will cover Gorton and Abbey Hey for 48 hours as of 1pm today (November 5) until 1pm on Saturday (November 7) It allows officers, who will be on patrol in the area, to direct people involved in or suspected of anti-social behaviour to leave the area for a specified period The force said the order for Gorton and Abbey Hey has been put in place due to concerns over 'the potential for bonfire-night related anti-social behaviour', which is said to have occurred 'in recent years' The area encompasses land between Ashton Old Road, Cornwall Street, Chapman Street, the A57/ Hyde Road, and across Debdale Park, Gorton Reservoir and Fairfield Golf Club

candidates.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney Thank you and goodbye, Pat Karney: 'Mr Manchester' makes his final journey through the city he loved with a visit, of course, to the Christmas Markets Prime Minister Andy Burnham delivered an emotional eulogy as friends, family a Add to preferred sources News Dianne Bourne Lifestyle Editor 16:21, 05 Nov 2026 He spent his life championing Manchester and was the leader of the city's Christmas celebrations. It was a fitting final journey for councillor Pat Karney, through the city streets he loved, before he Pat's funeral cortege was granted special permission to pause outside Manchester Town Hall, a place where he served the people of the city for the past 50 years and where the Christmas Markets he so loyally promoted every year are about to open As well-wishers looked on, Pat's funeral car was led through Albert Square with Sale MP Mike Kane playing Amazing Grace on the bagpipes. It was one of the many touching moments organised as part of an extraordinary send-off for the man affectionately known as Mr Manchester and Mr Council bosses arranged for a special emblem on the Big Wheel to say "Thank you Pat", while the city's advertising boards all flashed up with the same message throughout Thursday - complete with the huge Zippy Santa that Pat had so loved. Irish flags were also flying on Albert Sq Political leaders including Manchester MPs Lucy Powell, Graham Stringer, Jonathan Reynolds and Afzal Khan, Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig and former council leader Sir Richard Leese then assembled at Manchester's Hidden Gem church to pay their respects to the political legend

Before dawn broke, cops started smashing down doors Suspected ringleaders of a gang that has allegedly been shipping stolen cars in containers to the Democratic Republic of Officers from Greater Manchester Police (GMP) this morning (Wednesday, November 4) carried out dawn raids at a storage unit and three residential addresses in Oldham and Harpurhey , north Manchester It followed intelligence that a gang has been using 'sophisticated' electronic devices to hack locking systems in order to get into and steal high-powered cars across the UK. It is believed they have then been sending them as far afield as the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) i Seven international shipments have so far been successfully intercepted, leading to the recovery of 19 stolen vehicles, worth almost £600,000, which are suspected to be linked to this one crime group "It is a lucrative market," Detective Chief Superintendent Lewis Hughes told the Manchester Evening News, which accompanied officers as they executed the warrants under the cover of darkness View 3 Images Officers breaking down the door of one of the raided addresses (Image: GMP)

Credit: Transport for Greater Manchester Tram passengers in Greater Manche No trams will run at all on the Altrincham, Trafford Centre and Eccles lines from Monday 19 October to Sunday 1 November Meanwhile, between the same dates, services on the East Didsbury and Manchester Airport lines will terminate at Firswood, with a replacement bus service taking passengers into the city centre Also during this two-week period, services operating on the Rochdale line will terminate at Exchange Square All of these service changes will allow around 4km of tram track between Trafford Bar and Deansgate-Castlefield to be replaced, which is part of a £150m programme of investment Bee Network bosses also say the work will allow further speed restrictions to be lifted, leading to quicker and more reliable journeys

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester doesn’t do half measures when it comes to weather. You can leave the house in sunshine, get rained on outside Piccadilly and be rattled by a wind tunnel on Deansgate before you’ve reached the end of the road. It’s no surprise, then, that the hoodie is basically a local Those opinions are getting louder. Merch tables at the Albert Hall and the Ritz, clothing labels with one eye on the terraces, student societies, coffee shops in the Northern Quarter with a logo to show off. They all want something people will actually wear on a miserable Tuesday Which is why a lot of small labels start with heavyweight blank hoodies before they go anywhere near their own artwork. A thicker fabric holds warmth better, sits properly on the body and gives a print or embroidered logo a solid base. It’s less glamorous than talking about the d It’s about perception, too. Pick up a hoodie with a bit of heft and you assume the brand has put some thought into it. Pick up a flimsy one and you assume it hasn’t, however good the graphic is Weight, usually quoted in grams per square metre, is the number everyone fixates on, but it’s only part of the story. A good hoodie also needs a decent hood lining, ribbing that doesn’t give up after a few washes and seams that sit flat. Order a sample or two, wear them for a wee Think about fit as well. Manchester’s customers range from students who want something roomy to people in their forties who’d like a cut that doesn’t look like pyjamas. A spread of sizes, and ideally a couple of fits, saves a lot of awkward returns later on

You can leave the house in sunshine, get rained on outside Piccadilly and be rattled by a wind tunnel on Deansgate before you’ve reached the end of the road. It’s no surprise, then, that the hoodie is basically a local Those opinions are getting louder. Merch tables at the Albert Hall and the Ritz, clothing labels with one eye on the terraces, student societies, coffee shops in the Northern Quarter with a logo to show off. They all want something people will actually wear on a miserable Tuesday Which is why a lot of small labels start with heavyweight blank hoodies before they go anywhere near their own artwork. A thicker fabric holds warmth better, sits properly on the body and gives a print or embroidered logo a solid base. It’s less glamorous than talking about the d It’s about perception, too. Pick up a hoodie with a bit of heft and you assume the brand has put some thought into it. Pick up a flimsy one and you assume it hasn’t, however good the graphic is Weight, usually quoted in grams per square metre, is the number everyone fixates on, but it’s only part of the story. A good hoodie also needs a decent hood lining, ribbing that doesn’t give up after a few washes and seams that sit flat. Order a sample or two, wear them for a wee Think about fit as well. Manchester’s customers range from students who want something roomy to people in their forties who’d like a cut that doesn’t look like pyjamas. A spread of sizes, and ideally a couple of fits, saves a lot of awkward returns later on

candidates.lead: The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £
candidates.evidence_text: The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. A spokesperson said the scale of the liability was "significant" The Department of Housing, Communities and Local Government brought a case to a specialist tribunal, seeking an order for the developer to contribute towards the cost of the works paid from the taxpayer-supported fund On Thursday, the tribunal ruled that more than £45.7m should be paid to the government by Urban Splash Judge Jonathan Holbrook, sitting with two other First Tier Tribunal members, said in a 260-page judgment there was a "powerful case" for the developer "rather than the taxpayer, to bear the remediation costs"

The investment-led Greater Manchester Clean But while good progress has been made, the Council wants to go further because environmental air pollution remains a real health risk, especially for people in more disadvantaged communities or with existing health conditions who can be more vulnerable to its effects The Vision is simple: “Manchester will be a city where everyone can breathe cleaner air and live healthier lives.” Alongside it sits a headline action plan which will guide further measures to improve air quality across the city, based around four priorities Reduce people’s exposure to air pollution, prioritising the most vulnerable such as children and people with existing health conditions and communities where the potential health benefits are the greatest

candidates.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience

candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026 The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts foll Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show

Rochdale BID also secured gold and won the Best Business Improvement Distr Hampton by Hilton hotel entered for the first time this year, taking gold and category winner, alongside a gold for nearby Norton Grange hotel in the Large Accommodation category

evidence_packet.title: Litter and leaves swept up by new investment - Bolton Council
evidence_packet.lead: Streets in Bolton are set to be cleaner after the council invested in new equipment to tackle litter, leaves and fly-tipping
evidence_packet.summary: Streets in Bolton are set to be cleaner after the council invested in new equipment to tackle litter, leaves and fly-tipping
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Streets in Bolton are set to be cleaner after the council invested in new equipment to tackle litter, leaves and fly-tipping New road sweepers have been purchased, bigger bins installed at key spots and handy equipment stores provided for volunteer litter pickers A fleet of road sweepers in various sizes are used by the council to remove leaves and litter, and there have been several recent additions One large sweeper has been added, making three in total, and these are vital for keeping roads and drains clear of leaves and twigs in autumn, which reduces the risk of flooding as well as keeping streets looking tidy Six smaller mechanical sweepers are used on pavements, with teams focusing on different areas of Bolton on a rotating schedule A new electrically powered pavement sweeper has also been brought in that can get into smaller spaces like cycle lanes, helping to keep them clean and safe to use

candidates.lead: Pupils across Bolton returning from the summer holidays last month were greeted by safer and warmer classrooms after the council invested in the borough’s schools
candidates.evidence_text: Pupils across Bolton returning from the summer holidays last month were greeted by safer and warmer classrooms after the council invested in the borough’s schools Working with local employers Seddon, the council oversaw repairs and improvements at more than half a dozen schools, benefitting over 3,000 pupils from primary to secondary age The wide-ranging work was carried out over the summer break to minimise disruption The project saw some schools receiving new boilers and water heaters, new roof installed at one primary school, while another had more energy efficient windows installed Some fire alarm systems and emergency lighting have also been upgraded It is the second school decarbonisation project Seddon has delivered with Bolton Council, helping to improve the efficiency and long-term sustainability of school buildings across the borough

Alongside the new road, which is planned to be approximately 2.5 miles long, the proposals include significant investment in active travel infrastructure as well as enhanced access to existing paths, new crossing facilities, new or upgraded junctions, and a new bridge structure c The feedback from the public consultation will inform the development of the Wigan to Hindley Link Road, before an outline business case is submitted to the Department for Transport

candidates.evidence_text: Acumen Waste Service Limited have started preparatory works to remove the illegally deposited waste at Bolton House Road Following a robust tender process, Wigan Council announced that it had chosen Acumen as its preferred contractor last month, with contracts now officially signed after a compulsory standstill period Acumen is bringing in equipment and clearing vegetation at the Bickershaw site to allow waste to start being removed in the coming weeks Councillor Nazia Rehman, Leader of Wigan Council, said: “The contract signing and mobilisation at Bolton House Road is a clear sign of progress and a significant moment for the community who have had to deal with the impact of the illegal waste site “Reaching this stage also demonstrates the commitment of the council and partners to deliver the necessary framework for waste clearance, but our work does not stop here “We will continue to work with residents to ensure their voice is heard in the future of the site and will continue to support the Environment Agency’s criminal investigation to make sure those responsible are held accountable for the damage and distress they have caused.”

Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.lead: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre […] The post Sona Jobarteh Tour appeared first on Band on the Wall
candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. evidence_packet.title: Beat the Jams Autumn season announced
evidence_packet.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

candidates.lead: New CGI images have revealed the evolving design of Manchester’s £500m Therme resort, as construction progresses towards its planned 2029 opening
candidates.evidence_text: Gaming Gaming studio signs Sheffield’s largest out of town office letting since 2024 Brand Kevin the Carrot goes on final mission for McCann Manchester Brand Yorkshire campervan maker wins marketing award as YouTube views top 650,000 New images reveal latest vision for Manchester The latest visuals show the development’s indoor and outdoor spaces, including a 53,000 sq ft wellbeing garden and a new public plaza intended to improve connections with the Bridgewater Canal Foundations for the resort’s three main zones are emerging at the 28-acre TraffordCity site, with installation of its first main pool scheduled to begin next week The images follow design revisions made after Sir Robert McAlpine was appointed to build the 680,000 sq ft complex. The changes aim to improve construction efficiency, visitor experience and connections with public transport, including Metrolink Two proposed multi-storey car parks have been removed to open up views across the resort, with around 1,400 parking spaces instead distributed across the site. Changes to the entrance and internal and external spaces are also intended to improve operational efficiency and manage A Section 73 planning application has been submitted covering amendments including the parking arrangements. Therme says the overall scale of the development remains unchanged following a reduction in size in 2024

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. READ MORE: ANS Group reports 500% RoI from latest AI deployment Students were more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI, including its ability to improve productivity, support learning and reduce workloads. The most prominent uses reported by students involved producing written text, finding answers to assignments, and translating or improving grammar. Staff varied considerably in their experience and expertise with AI, making it difficult for some to judge how students were using the technology. Researchers argue that universities need to move beyond treating AI primarily as a technical challenge or a threat to academic integrity, and develop a better understanding of how students and staff engage with it. The research examined how academic staff and students perceived their own use of generative AI tools, as well as their views of how the technology was being used in higher education. The study surveyed 45 academic staff and 86 students in a school covering social science disciplines at a UK research-intensive university. The questionnaires were conducted between April and June 2024, so essentially before AI took over the likes of Google whether you asked it to or not. When asked about students’ use of AI for academic purposes, staff gave an average rating of 5.23 on a seven-point scale. Students’ own responses produced an average of just 3.11. The researchers caution that students may have underreported their use of AI, but say the difference nevertheless points to the limited information staff may have about how students use these tools in their studies. AI use can be difficult for lecturers to identify, particularly when they see only the final version of an assignment rather than the process through which it was produced. Students may also use AI independently of their interactions with teaching staff, leaving academics with an incomplete picture of their working practices. The research also found that students were generally more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI. Students rated the technology more highly in terms of its likely contribution to academic performance, including helping them learn about their subjects, increasing productivity and reducing workloads. They also felt more strongly than staff that appropriate conditions and support were in place to help them use AI tools. Among the uses identified in the survey, students reported using generative AI to find answers to questions and assignments, generate written work, and translate or improve the grammar of their writing. The researchers suggest that the immediate appeal of AI tools may lie in their ability to produce and improve text. However, they also argue that universities need to understand the range of ways students use the technology, rather than assume that its role in academic work is straightforward. The study also found considerable variation in staff members’ familiarity with AI. While 63 per cent of academic staff respondents had used at least one generative AI tool in the six months before the survey, some had limited practical experience of the technology. By bringing origination, underwriting and monitoring together, Crediflow aims to reduce repeated work and help lenders grow their loan books without an associated increase in administrative costs. candidates.evidence_text: US giant NetApp completes acquisition of Manchester’s Peak AIO Posted on November 6, 2026 by staff US giant NetApp completes acquisition of Manchester’s Peak AIO Nasdaq-listed data platform swoops for firm addressing industry's most demanding data-intensive computing challenges Share: Listen to article Deals Nasdaq-listed US giant NetApp has completed its acquisition of Manchester AI firm PEAK AIO. PEAK AIO was founded in Manchester by Mark Klarzynski and was designed to address some of the industry’s most demanding data-intensive computing challenges. The company’s core innovation, a next-generation metadata architecture and high-performance parallel file system, was developed to solve one of the defining infrastructure challenges of the AI era: enabling shared storage to scale alongside the GPU clusters that power modern AI workloads. The deal, for an undisclosed amount, has now secured regulatory approvals. Investor Pembroke VCT plc, a London-listed venture capital trust, said it would generate a significant return for shareholders. “NetApp and PEAK:AIO were built around the shared conviction that the AI era needs data infrastructure designed to scale to extraordinary levels,” said Mark Klarzynski, chief technology officer and founder at PEAK:AIO. “With the acquisition by NetApp, we can bring our innovation together with the reach, expertise, and trusted customer relationships of a global data infrastructure leader. Together, we are well positioned to help define what comes next and deliver technology that makes managing data for the AI era more practical, efficient, and accessible.” £178m ticketing giant Skiddle secures first external investment Syam Nair, chief product officer at NetApp, added: “The AI factory is only as productive as its data pipeline. By combining NetApp’s unified storage with PEAK:AIO’s metadata architecture, we separate metadata from data so performance scales out with concurrency, and we do it with open standards rather than proprietary clients. “Customers can run more AI workloads, on their existing infrastructure, with the security, resilience, and simplicity of enterprise data management.” George Kurian, CEO at NetApp, said: “AI infrastructure is reaching unprecedented scale, demanding a new approach to storage built from the ground up. “By combining PEAK:AIO’s expertise in metadata services and parallel namespace innovation with the proven scale, data management capabilities, and enterprise-grade services of the NetApp Platform, we are leapfrogging the market as we deliver our next-generation, zettabyte-scale architecture to support the growth of AI clouds and GPU-as-a-service providers.” New images reveal latest plans for £500m Therme Manchester Related Stories View All Could AI firm’s director be key to Poundland rescue bid? evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new five-floor bar, kitchen, record store and club is set to open on Deansgate this month Resident will take over the historic building nestled between The Lost Dene and the Sawyers Arms, with bosses saying the new concept has been crafted around the city’s underground music culture The concept will open in stages throughout the next year, with the first phase set to launch on Thu 12 Nov. Kicking things off will be Electric Pizza Shop, a red-lit room built around a DJ booth, serving pizza both by the slice and by the box, alongside classic cocktails and hous After dark, the basement and ground floor transform into a club, with Resident promising a DJ lineup chosen ‘for the quality of their selections, the crowd they bring and the culture around them, not for their follower counts or what the data says.’ Each headliner will be paired with Resident’s own DJs, and visitors will be able to peruse and purchase records from those performing. The first season of parties is free, with guest list sign-up through the venue’s website, running Thursday to Saturday The core residents are Urbi, Shimrise, Groove Division, Joe Roche, Bay, SUI 13, Rhod Parry, Jacinta, Jordan Villa, Pez and Maclo, covering everything from Chicago and deep house to percussive Latin house, garage and acid

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
